To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the O(n3) minimization of clock constraints is an effective technique for space reduction in the state-space representation of networks of timed automata; (2) static analysis of control structures can be used to reduce the space-usage in an on-the fly algorithm; (3) the two techniques complement each other, and can be used simultaneously.

The state-space explosion problem in model-checking of real-time systems can be significantly reduced by using a combination of two orthogonal techniques: a compact data structure based on a novel algorithm for minimizing the number of clock constraints in a system, and an on-the-fly technique for reducing the number of states by static analysis of the structure of the system.
the two techniques, the compact data structure and on-the-fly state-space reduction, can be combined to give a truly significant space-saving for model checking real-time systems.
